outcome: composition of infant gut and nose microbiota
cohort: 42 mother-infant pairs from the GUSTO birth cohort
finding: While maternal rectal microbiota was more similar to infant gut microbiota than maternal vaginal microbiota, a large proportion of infant microbiota could not be identified in maternal microbiota, suggesting other sources contribute to infant gut and nasal microbiota development.
mod_finding: The study confirmed a clear difference in microbiota between infants born by Caesarean section compared to vaginally delivered infants, suggesting factors beyond reduced transfer of maternal vaginal microbes contribute to this difference.
